channel.title: Onchain Brief
channel.description: Crypto news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, DeFi, stablecoins, exchanges, wallets, security incidents, regulation and new blockchain networks.

item.title: How to Swap Bridged Crypto Into a Deposit Token
item.description: Bridged tokens often need one more swap before they can be deposited; compare the net quote, check the destination token, and confirm the protocol accepts it.

item.title: Three receipt checks for Mantle bridge fees
item.description: A bridge receipt shows whether a transaction ran and its gas cost, but three checks confirm the network, fee and final token movement before you stop.

item.title: When Is a Bridge Arrival Really Final?
item.description: A bridge arrival is usable only after the destination chain records it and the bridge’s own checks pass; those steps can take longer than a wallet update.

item.title: How to Reach a Token Market on Another Network
item.description: To reach a token market on another blockchain, move funds onto that network first or use a cross-chain swap, then check the token and route before signing.

item.title: Bridge deposit quotes have no standard expiry
item.description: A bridge quote’s timer is set by the service and may expire before its deposit address does, so check the deadline, rate terms and order status before sending funds.

item.title: Minimum received sets the floor for a crypto swap
item.description: Minimum received sets the least output a swap can deliver before it fails, giving traders a clear price floor while leaving room for market movement during execution.

item.title: What Support Needs to Check When a Wallet Swap Is Delayed
item.description: A delayed wallet swap is easier to trace when support gets the transaction hash, both networks, and the exact stage where progress stopped, before you retry.

item.title: How to join a token sale on Mantle
item.description: Joining a token sale on Mantle means using the project’s sale page, funding a compatible wallet, checking the rules and claiming tokens after the sale.

item.title: How crypto treasuries can rebalance across chains
item.description: Market moves can leave a crypto treasury overweight on one chain; a measured rebalance weighs target holdings against fees, liquidity, timing and route risk.

item.title: What to Do With a Pending Swap During a Token Migration
item.description: A pending swap may be waiting on the network, a bridge, or a new token contract. Check its status before you retry, cancel, or move funds.

item.title: A bridge-and-swap route moves crypto in one flow
item.description: A bridge-and-swap route moves value to another blockchain and trades it into a chosen token, combining two steps while adding fees, timing, and trust choices.

item.title: What an Intermediate Asset Costs in a Wallet Swap
item.description: An intermediate asset can help a wallet find a swap route, but its cost shows up in the final amount through pool fees, price impact and network charges.

item.title: How BNB Chain Tokens Reach Ethereum Liquidity
item.description: Moving tokens from BNB Chain to Ethereum means choosing a route, checking destination liquidity and fees, and confirming which asset will arrive in your wallet.

item.title: Exchange deposit memos need a clear path across chains
item.description: An exchange memo can route a deposit to the right account, but a bridge may not carry it across chains; check the final network, address and tag before sending.

item.title: How to move gaming proceeds into another game's tokens
item.description: Gaming proceeds can fund another game, but only after you match the token, network and fees; this guide explains the swap path and the checks to make first.

item.title: Recheck the Swap Quote After a Wallet Session Expires
item.description: If a wallet session expires during a swap, reconnecting does not confirm the old quote is still usable; check the amount, route and fees again before signing.

item.title: How to turn crypto into a restaking position
item.description: A restaking position starts with an asset the protocol accepts, then adds a service and operator choice; check conversion costs, exit terms and added risk.

item.title: Five steps to fund an Ethereum validator
item.description: A validator deposit starts with 32 ETH, prepared keys and a synced node; these five steps cover the Launchpad, wallet transfer and what happens next.

item.title: Compare Cross-Chain Routes by What Arrives
item.description: Compare cross-chain routes by the amount that should arrive, the time estimate, and the fees each route takes, then check the destination token before sending.

item.title: Ledger says hidden chips sent CryptoBilis wallet phrases over LTE
item.description: Ledger says hidden hardware in some CryptoBilis-sold wallets copied 24-word recovery phrases during setup and sent them over LTE, putting buyers’ crypto at risk.
